---
title: "The Chicago Anchor Dataset"
subtitle: "Real crime data we'll use all semester"
---

Most lecture examples this semester use **one real dataset** — reported crime in Chicago during 2025, from the [Chicago Police Department's public data portal](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Public-Safety/Crimes-2001-to-Present/ijzp-q8t2) — so that each new technique builds on data you already know. It comes at **two levels**:

## 1. Incident level — `chicago-crimes-2025.csv`

A random sample of **30,000** of the 237,472 crimes reported to CPD in 2025 (sampled with `set.seed(705)`).

```r
crimes <- read_csv("https://smourtgos.github.io/crju705/data/chicago-crimes-2025.csv")
```

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `id` | numeric | CPD incident ID |
| `date` | date | Date the incident occurred |
| `hour` | numeric | Hour of day (0–23) |
| `primary_type` | character | CPD primary offense classification (THEFT, BATTERY, …) |
| `description` | character | More detailed offense description |
| `location_description` | character | Type of location (STREET, RESIDENCE, …) |
| `crime_category` | character | Violent / Property / Other (course-defined, see below) |
| `arrest` | logical | Did the incident result in an arrest? |
| `domestic` | logical | Domestic-related incident (per Illinois DV statute) |
| `community_area` | numeric | Chicago community area number (1–77) |
| `community` | character | Community area name |
| `latitude`, `longitude` | numeric | Anonymized block-level coordinates (may be missing) |

**`crime_category` definitions (course convention):** Violent = homicide, criminal sexual assault, robbery, battery, assault. Property = burglary, theft, motor vehicle theft, arson. Everything else = Other.

## 2. Community-area level — `chicago-areas.csv`

All 237,472 incidents (not just the sample) aggregated to Chicago's **77 community areas**, joined with socioeconomic measures from the [CMAP Community Data Snapshots](https://cmap.illinois.gov/data/community-data-snapshots/) (American Community Survey estimates).

```r
areas <- read_csv("https://smourtgos.github.io/crju705/data/chicago-areas.csv")
```

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `community_area`, `community` | id | Area number (1–77) and name |
| `population` | numeric | Total population (ACS) |
| `crimes_total`, `crimes_violent`, `crimes_property` | numeric | 2025 reported crime counts |
| `crime_rate`, `violent_rate`, `property_rate` | numeric | Crimes per 1,000 residents |
| `high_violence` | logical | Violent-crime rate above the citywide median? |
| `arrest_rate` | numeric | Share of the area's 2025 incidents ending in arrest |
| `median_age` | numeric | Median age |
| `pct_white`, `pct_black`, `pct_hispanic`, `pct_asian` | numeric | Racial/ethnic composition (%) |
| `unemployment_rate` | numeric | Unemployed share of the labor force (%) |
| `pct_bachelors` | numeric | Adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher (%) |
| `pct_no_hs_diploma` | numeric | Adults 25+ without a high-school diploma (%) |
| `median_income` | numeric | Median household income ($) |
| `income_per_capita` | numeric | Per-capita income ($) |
| `pct_renter` | numeric | Renter-occupied share of households (%) |
| `pct_vacant` | numeric | Vacant share of housing units (%) |
| `median_rent` | numeric | Median gross rent ($) |

## Important caveats — we will return to these all semester

- **Reported** crime only. These data reflect crimes *reported to and recorded by* CPD — not all crime that occurred. Reporting rates differ across offense types and communities.
- **An arrest is not a conviction**, and `arrest_rate` reflects incident clearance patterns, not "guilt rates."
- The ACS measures are **survey estimates** with sampling error, larger for smaller areas.
- Aggregate (community-level) associations do **not** license conclusions about individuals — we'll name this properly (the *ecological fallacy*) when we get to correlation.

## Provenance

Snapshot pulled July 2026; build script archived in the course repository (`R/build-anchor-dataset.R`) so the dataset is exactly reproducible. Sources: [Chicago Data Portal, Crimes 2001–present](https://data.cityofchicago.org/Public-Safety/Crimes-2001-to-Present/ijzp-q8t2) (dataset `ijzp-q8t2`) and [CMAP Community Data Snapshots 2026](https://cmap.illinois.gov/data/community-data-snapshots/) (CCA table).
